name: hobbyhorse

attributes.attribute: a puppet of a horse worn by a man in parades at British festivals
a possible remnant of early religious ceremonies
thought to derive from Celtic practice, perhaps linked to the horse goddess Epona

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The hobbyhorse is a British folkloric figure. Many folkloric events may descend from early religious ceremonies. The hobbyhorse is one such remnant. It is a puppet of a horse worn by a man in parades at British festivals. The syllable hob often marks a link to the Otherworld. So scholars think the hobbyhorse comes from Celtic practice. It may relate to Epona, the horse goddess.
objective: Document the hobbyhorse as a British folkloric figure.
